Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 52042 of 2022

Applicant :- Dharmendra @ Dharma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Mahendra Pratap,Abhishek Kumar Jaiswal,Amit Daga,Anurag Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Jawahir Yadav
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
01.

Heard Shri Amit Daga, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Jawahir Yadav, learned counsel for the
first informant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

02. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant seeking bail in case crime no.381 of
2022, under Sections 420, 406, 419,467,468,471 and 411 I.P.C. and Section 66 D I.T. Act, P.S.
Pilkhuwa, District Hapur.

03.  As per version in the F.I.R, from certain mobile number a person who named himself as Raj Kumar Mishra called the first informant Varkita Khandelwal; he told the first informant that he is employee of Governing Body of Insurance Council and said that her LIC agent has defrauded her and has deliberately got her LIC bonous cancelled which is otherwise payable to the customers regularly; he said that she should get NOC of Rs.18484/-.

It is mentioned in the F.I.R. that the person on the other side of the mobile was having all the knowledge of her LIC policy, therefore, she believed him; he further told her that Governing Body of Insurance Council regularly deals with such kind of matters where agents defraud the customers; she has been deprived of silver and gold Dharmendra @ Dharma vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121447763/
1 bonus and that she is entitled for Rs.8,50,000/-; she has to deposit Rs.123550/- which shall be returned to her after 3% deducting therefrom; the caller cautioned her to keep things to herself and assured that all the money shall be transferred in her account by 7th December; all the things were verified from her by another person Satish Kaushik on another mobile; a month thereafter she was told that in such cases of exploitation by the agent the customers is entitled for government I.P.O.;
she could not realise that she is being defrauded; she arranged for money from her sisters, brothers and friends and transferred Rs.45 lacs in different accounts shown as accounts of GBIC; certificates of payments were sent to her; when the time for maturity came she was told that said Raj Kumar Mishra had expired in accident, therefore, a new file manager shall be deputed for processing her file; in the month of April she was informed that Satish was the new file Manager; and further that some rules and regulations have been changed, Therefore, she will have to pay 1% i.e. Rs.20900/-
for FNFS and again Rs.2 lacs 65 thousand as stamp duty and thereafter all the funds shall be transferred in her account; after a gap of 15 to 20 days there was new demand that in case she deposits 10%, she will gain some advantage as per the government rules and that she will be getting the money within three days of deposit thereof; she borrowed certain money from her relatives and deposited in different accounts all in the name of GBIC; when she enquired about the existence of different accounts in the name of GBIC; she was told that different accounts in the name of GBIC exist for different IPO; by the end of 15 June, 2022 she realized that she had already deposited Rs.7452935/- and she called the person concerned but her call was not picked up and she became suspicious; she went to the address which was shown on the papers and found that there was no such office and everything was fraudulent; however, meanwhile when she called Satish Kaushik her call was picked up; he said that her payments have been finalzied by them; she had realized that fraud has been committed with her, therefore, she recorded the conversation so that she can catch fraudesters and their locations could be traced.

sentences.text: During investigation it was found that the applicant acting as master mind was running a well organized scheme to cheat and dupe the vulnerable victim.
And was arrested.

Following contentions have been put before this Court by the applicant.
1.
The applicant is not named in the F.I.R. and has been falsely implicated in this case by the police.
2. Recovery of some mobile sets, ATM cards and cash of Rs.1,20,000/- has been shown by the police but there is nothing to connect him with the crime.
3. There is no evidence on record to establish that offence under Sections 420, 406, 419,467,468,471 and 411 I.P.C. and Section 66 D I.T. Act are made out.
Locations of B party cell phones were traced to other persons not to the applicant.

The applicant is arrested on the basis of confidential information; there is no evidence to establish that it was the applicant who had called on the first informant;or that he was one who had used the mobile from the numbers as mentioned in the F.I.R. or having surfaced during the investigation;
8. The complicity of the applicant accused is doubtful; he is in jail since last one year.

04. Application for bail is opposed with vehemence by learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the first informant highlighting a number of facts, circumstances and the arguments as below:-
i.

In this case a thorough investigation was conducted by cyber cell, Gautam Budh Nagar and enough material has been collected to establish that present applicant Dharmendra @ Dharma had in fact called the first informant on different occasions,
introduced himself with fake names and made her believe that she was the real office bearer in the GBIC.
ii. On his arrest NOKIA mobile with certain IMEI number was recovered from which different SIM cards were used.

She was called several times by those mobile numbers; two mobile numbers which were used by him have been traced to him and tallied with; this evidence is enough to show that he was the master mind behind the crime.
ii. After thorough investigation chargesheet has been submitted against him.
All the names used by phone callers were fake.
He was the master mind.

Complicity of one more co-accused Alok Jha besides a number of others has been found; the crime was committed in a well planned and organized manner and any indulgence on the part of the court may set at naught all the effort by the Investigating Officer.

iii. My attention has been drawn to several parcha of the case diary describing the facts and circumstances by which trail was followed leading to apprehension of accused/applicant.
iv.

The modus operandi adopted by the present applicant was to lift up the data from the internet and look for vulnerable candidate; in this case details of the first informant were procured from the website of Intermediate Educational Board; forged receipts were prepared by obtaining and downloading the formats from google.
They prepared the forged receipts by using editing Apps and that's how they got transferred about Rs.75 lac from the first informant 05.

I considered the nature of the accusations, the evidence collected, the role ascribed to the applicant; the manner of commission of crime; severity of punishment, the likely impact on the society; lack of any plausible or credible theory in defence and all other material facts and circumstances.
In my view, a case for bail is not made out.
06. Accordingly the bail application is rejected.
